references.text: The altar shall be most holy, and whatever touches it becomes holy - the same principle of consecration through contact
Moses anoints the burnt offering altar and consecrates it so that it becomes most holy
Moses sprinkles oil on the altar seven times to consecrate it - parallel to the seven-day inauguration
A seven-day period of inauguration for Aaron and his sons at the entrance of the tabernacle
Whatever touches the flesh of the sin offering becomes holy - the same principle of consecration by contact
For seven days they shall make atonement for the altar and cleanse it in Ezekiel's temple vision
Jesus asks what is greater, the gift or the altar that makes the gift holy - referring to the sanctifying power of the altar
Explains the concrete blood ritual necessary to achieve the atonement and consecration mentioned in the source verse.
Extends the principle of the altar's atonement to apply to the entire cultic system on the Day of Atonement.
